-- An appointment whose end time has passed is done. Marking it is what unlocks the review
-- ask, and it is deliberately based on ends_at, not starts_at: asking someone how their cut
-- went while they are still in the chair is worse than not asking.
WITH done AS (
  UPDATE appointment SET status = 'completed', updated_at = now()
  WHERE status = 'confirmed' AND ends_at < now() - interval '30 minutes'
  RETURNING id
)
SELECT json_build_object('completed', (SELECT count(*) FROM done)) AS result;

-- A review that warranted a human but whose manager copy never went out. 39 releases the
-- claim when a send fails, so the absence of a log row is the signal to try again. Without
-- this the feedback is stored and nobody ever reads it.
SELECT r.appointment_id, 'manager' AS recipient,
       'review_' || r.sentiment AS kind,
       format('%s for %s - %s on %s (%s), %s from %s:' || chr(10) || '"%s"',
              CASE WHEN r.sentiment = 'praise' THEN 'Praise' ELSE 'Complaint' END,
              st.name, sv.name,
              to_char(a.starts_at AT TIME ZONE 'Asia/Manila', 'Dy DD Mon, HH24:MI'),
              a.ref,
              CASE WHEN r.rating IS NULL THEN 'no rating' ELSE r.rating || '/5' END,
              c.name, COALESCE(r.comment, '(no comment left)')) AS text
FROM review r
JOIN appointment a ON a.id = r.appointment_id
JOIN stylist st ON st.id = a.stylist_id
JOIN service sv ON sv.id = a.service_id
JOIN client  c  ON c.id  = a.client_id
WHERE r.sentiment <> 'neutral'
  AND r.created_at > now() - interval '7 days'
  AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM notification_log n
                  WHERE n.appointment_id = r.appointment_id AND n.recipient = 'manager'
                    AND n.kind = 'review_' || r.sentiment);

-- Who to ask for a review: their own completed appointment, finished recently enough that
-- they remember it, not already asked, not already reviewed, and reachable.
--
-- The ask is written as a pending row — the same mechanism a booking read-back uses — but ONLY
-- when nothing else is already waiting on their answer. A review request that overwrites an
-- outstanding booking confirmation would turn their "yes" into the wrong thing entirely.
WITH cand AS (
  SELECT a.id, a.ref, a.client_id, sv.name AS service_name, st.name AS stylist_name,
         c.name AS client_name, c.channel || ':' || c.channel_user_id AS user_key,
         to_char(a.starts_at AT TIME ZONE 'Asia/Manila', 'Dy DD Mon') AS when_local
  FROM appointment a
  JOIN service sv ON sv.id = a.service_id
  JOIN stylist st ON st.id = a.stylist_id
  JOIN client  c  ON c.id  = a.client_id
  JOIN bot_user_profile b ON b.user_key = c.channel || ':' || c.channel_user_id
  WHERE a.status = 'completed'
    AND a.ends_at > now() - interval '7 days'          -- nobody remembers a haircut from March
    -- Salon hours only. An appointment that ended at 20:00 gets asked the next morning, not
    -- at three in the morning because that is when the scheduler happened to come round.
    AND EXTRACT(HOUR FROM (now() AT TIME ZONE 'Asia/Manila')) BETWEEN 9 AND 19
    AND COALESCE(btrim(c.channel_user_id), '') <> ''
    AND (b.pending_booking IS NULL OR b.pending_set_at < now() - interval '30 minutes')
    AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM review r WHERE r.appointment_id = a.id)
    AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM notification_log n
                    WHERE n.appointment_id = a.id AND n.recipient = 'client'
                      AND n.recipient_ref = a.client_id AND n.kind = 'review_request')
  ORDER BY a.ends_at DESC
), asked AS (
  UPDATE bot_user_profile b
     SET pending_booking = json_build_object('kind', 'review', 'ref', cand.ref,
           'appointment_id', cand.id, 'service_name', cand.service_name,
           'stylist_name', cand.stylist_name,
           'summary', 'review ' || cand.ref)::jsonb,
         pending_set_at = now(), updated_at = now()
    FROM cand WHERE b.user_key = cand.user_key
  RETURNING b.user_key, cand.id
)
SELECT cand.id AS appointment_id, 'client' AS recipient, 'review_request' AS kind,
       format('Hi %s — how was your %s with %s on %s? A rating out of 5 and a line about it would really help. '
              || 'Reply here whenever you have a moment.',
              cand.client_name, cand.service_name, cand.stylist_name, cand.when_local) AS text
FROM asked JOIN cand ON cand.id = asked.id;

parameters.content:
## 40 · ask for a review

Marks appointments complete 30 minutes after they end — asking how the cut went while someone is still in the chair is worse than not asking — then asks that customer, once, guarded by `notification_log`.

The ask is written as a pending row, the same mechanism a booking read-back uses, and **only when nothing else is waiting on their answer**: a review request that overwrote an outstanding booking confirmation would turn their "yes" into the wrong thing entirely.

Nobody is chased about a haircut from three months ago, and nobody is asked twice.
